newsitem.title: USA: HF Ahmanson bids for Great Western - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: HF Ahmanson bids for Great Western - WSJ.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson has made a hostile bid for Great Western Financial Corp valued at nearly $6 billion in stock, or about $42.53 a share, the Wall Street Journal said Tuesday.
The paper said people familiar with the situation say Ahmanson is offering 1.05 shares of its stock for each share of Great Western.
Ahmanson, the nation's largest thrift, closed at 40-1/2 Friday. Great Western, the nation's second-largest thrift, closed at 34-1/4. Monday was a holiday.
The paper said Ahmanson's chairman and chief executive, Charles Rinehart, gave a letter outlining the proposal to Great Western President and Chief Executive John Maher yesterday.
Neither company was immediately available for comment.
The combination of the companies, both based in Los Angeles, would create one of the biggest financial institutions in California with assets of $93 billion, the paper said.
